description.narrative:
The overall aim of the project is to advance knowledge and generate new evidence that can enhance the performance of the UN system when it comes to managing the risks posed by climate change in fragile and conflict affected countries, and the achievement of the sustainable development goals.
The objective of the project is to produce evidenced-based information and analysis on the climate-related peace and security risks of specific countries and regions on the agenda of the UN Security Council. In 2025 NUPI/SIPRI will develop factsheets on the interlinkages between climate change and conflict in South Sudan, Haiti and Lake Chad related to UNOWAS to support the UN system during Denmark’s tenure in the UNSC (2025-2026).
The Norwegian Institute of International Affairs (NUPI) and the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) contribute to generating evidenced-based research on CPS risks for countries on the UNSC agenda, as well as related research on the impact of climate change on the ability of the UN to achieve the SDGs, including SDG 16, as well as its conflict prevention, mediation, peacekeeping and peacebuilding mandated tasks. In this regard, NUPI and SIPRI will also undertake research into the effectiveness of the implementation of country-level CPS-related programming, with the aim of help affected countries, their partners and the UN system learn from their experiences and to develop a body of knowledge based on best practices and lessons gained.
